title: TasksExport
description: tasks-export/1: every document tasks.nvim hands to a machine. One of the kinds below, told apart by `kind`. The engine writes exactly these fields (a field that is not listed fails the contract tests); a reader ignores fields it does not know, because inside one version the contract only grows.

MeetingEntry.description: One meeting (`<area>/MEETINGS/<slug>.md`). A broken meeting is still here (`valid: false`, `problems`); a field that is missing is unknown. Nothing changes with the day: whether a meeting is past is for the reader to say from `starts_at` and `ends_at` (local wall time, or the time of `tz`).

status.description: Absent for a file with no valid status.

end.description: The end as written (`end:`), when the file names one.

starts_at.description: `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM`, or the day of an all-day meeting.

ends_at.description: The end in the same form (an all-day meeting: its last day).

tz.description: An IANA time zone the times are written in (only its form is checked).

notify_set.description: Only when the file names `notify`: then an empty `notify` means no notice; without it the vault's default applies.

image.description: The old name of `cover`, kept for the readers of before: the same value.

repeat.description: A series (capability `meeting_series`): its interval as the routines write it (`1w`, `2w`, `1m`; `daily`, `weekly`, `monthly`, `yearly` are read as `1d`, `1w`, `1m`, `1y`). A series is the template of its occurrences: `meetings` lists the occurrences, not the series.

repeat_until.description: A series: its last possible day.

except.description: A series: the days without an occurrence, in order.

series.description: An occurrence of a series: the id of the series.

occurrence.description: An occurrence of a series: its day in the series (the day in its slug `<slug of the series>-<day>`; `date` differs when it was moved).

virtual.description: An occurrence without a file yet, computed from the series: `etag` is the version of the series file, `file` the file it gets on the first entry (an operation on its id makes it).

Meetings.description: tasks.meetings: the meetings whose days touch the window `since`..`until`, the earliest first, one page. Capability `meetings`.

undated.description: Meetings that match but have no valid date: in no window.

PathHours.description: Hours of a path or a session: planned (`{h=N}`, `{h=N-M}` on the outermost point that carries it: an inner one is part of it), done (`{done_h=N}`, the outermost too) and open (the planned hours of the points not closed, less what was done on each, never below 0). A point whose leaves are all dropped plans nothing; optional points count for nothing. Two decimal places at most.

LearnPoint.description: A learning point as the learning views over all paths carry it: where it stands, its stage (the root it stands below) and what its marks say.

index.description: Position in document order (`PathNode.index`); `#<index>` names the point where it has no key.

stage_index.description: The `index` of the root it stands below (its own for a root).

promoted.description: The task the point was promoted to.

h_min.description: Planned hours (`{h=N}` or the lower end of `{h=N-M}`).

safety.description: The point is `{safety}` or below one: closing it needs `ack`.

machine.description: The machines the point may be practised on; absent: every machine.

LearnNext.description: tasks.learn_next: for every running learning path (stage `doing`, or `idle` with its project's `status: doing`) the first `n` points (default 3) that may be learned now, in document order: open (not blocked), not optional, on the machine when one is asked for. Only paths with such a point; `doing` before `idle`, then the most recently active first (the last day the series of the learning figures saw a change, else `updated`), then by id. Capability `learn_next`.

machine.description: The machine asked for; absent: every machine.

LearnNotes.description: tasks.learn_notes: the points of all learning paths that carry a note (`> ` lines), a link or an image, narrowed to a `kind` and a search text (`query`: a part of the label, the note or the link, without case), each with its path, stage and state; open paths by id, then with `include_done` the finished ones, each in document order. At most `limit` (default 200); `total` counts every hit. Capability `learn_notes`.

path_done.description: The path is finished (from a Backlog, `include_done`).

note.description: The `> ` lines below the point, joined by newlines (Markdown, untrusted).

image.description: A file below `assets/` of the path; a client draws it as an image only.

CompetenceLevel.description: A stage of the scale of the competences, 0 (unknown) to 8 (mastermind), in halves (3.5: the evidence for 4 begun).

CompetenceTarget.description: Stages aimed at, in theory (`t`) and practice (`p`); a target written as one stage holds for both.

Competences.description: tasks.competences: the fields of knowledge of the vault (`<area>/ROADMAP/competences/<slug>.md`), each with its stage in theory (`t`) and practice (`p`; absent: not assessed, `?`), its targets in 12 and 24 months, the day it was assessed, its text (untrusted, cut at 16 KiB) and the open learning paths that name it (`competence:`), plus the scale (0..8 with the names of the stages) in the language of the vault. A broken file is still here (`valid: false`, `problems`). Capability `competences`.

lang.description: The language of the names of the scale: the vault's (`tasks-vault.json`), else German.

body.description: The text after the frontmatter, trimmed (Markdown, untrusted): why, and the next evidence.

paths.description: The open learning paths that name it, by id.

LearnEvidence.description: tasks.learn_evidence: the evidence of all learning paths: the points whose label starts with `Nachweis:`, `Aufgabe:` or `Ergebnis:` (`Evidence:`, `Result:`), each with its path, the competences the path serves, its stage, state, link and the stage of the competence scale it proves (`{for=t4}`). Narrowed to the paths that serve `competence`, to areas and paths; with `include_done` the finished paths too. Open paths by id, then the finished ones, each in document order. Capability `learn_evidence`.

path_done.description: The path is finished (from a Backlog, `include_done`).

label.description: As written (Markdown, untrusted), the word `Nachweis:` and the like included.

state.description: The state shown (`PathNode.derived`): `learned` is evidence given.

link.description: The first link of the label: where the evidence lies.

for.description: The stage it proves (`{for=t4}`): `t` theory or `p` practice.

LearnStepFigures.description: What changed in a step: points learned, seen and dropped, XP earned and hours done (differences of the series, may be negative when a mark was taken back).

LearnHistory.description: tasks.learn_history: what the series of the learning figures (`_Telemetry/history/learn-YYYY-MM.jsonl`, one row per day and path, written by `history_record`, `tasks history record` and `tasks index`) says over a window `since`..`until` in steps of a `day`, `week` (from Monday) or `month`. The series exists from the day it was introduced: a step before its first day (`first`) is absent, never 0; without any row there are no `points`, no `first`, no `streak`. A path's first row on the first day of the series is where it starts (nothing learned that day); a path that appears later counts from nothing. Capability `learn_history`.

first.description: The first day of the series in the scope.

streak.description: Learning days in a row (a day on which a point was learned or seen): `current` the run that ends on `until` or the day before (today not learned yet keeps it), `longest` the longest run since `first`, `last_day` the last learning day.

points.description: One per step from the step of `first` on, `date` its first day: the sums over the paths, `days` the learning days of the step, `paths` the paths that changed in it (with the level reached at its end).

paths.description: Every path of the scope with a row, by id: its first row, the last day something changed (up to `until`), the level at `until`, the day each level was first reached (`ref` as `PathLevel.ref`) and each reward first granted, and once the series reaches four weeks back the pace of those weeks (`points` closed and `hours` done per week) and `forecast_weeks`: the weeks the open points (and open hours, `hours_min`/`hours_max`) of an open path take at that pace (absent at a pace of 0).

title.description: The title of the path as it is now (open or finished); absent when it is gone.

incomplete.description: Lines and files of the series that were skipped, relative to the vault.

Milestones.description: tasks.milestones: the milestones of the vault or of an area (`<area>/ROADMAP/milestones/`), each with its progress over its members. Capability `milestones`.

MilestoneDocument.description: tasks.milestone: one milestone with its body, its members (kind, state, what each counts), the lines of its `## Verlauf` and the members that are in it twice. Capability `milestone`.

body.description: The file after the frontmatter, untrusted text.

members.description: The members in the order of `includes`.

kind.description: What the id names: a member (`task`, `plan`, `project`, `path`, `meeting`) or a fault (`milestone`: another milestone; `unknown`: nothing; `foreign`: an id of another vault; `bad`: no `<area>/<slug>`).

state.description: Only for a member: finished or not.

done.description: What it counts as done (a plan or project: its finished tasks).

total.description: What it counts in all (a plan or project: its tasks, at least one; a fault: 0).

history.description: The lines of `## Verlauf` (`YYYY-MM-DD reached`, `YYYY-MM-DD opened again: ...`), without the dash.

overlaps.description: Members that are in it twice: `id` is already part of `via`, a plan or project it names too.

MilestoneEntry.description: A milestone (`<area>/ROADMAP/milestones/<slug>.md`): the head of its file, its progress, whether it is overdue, its version.

reached.description: The day it was reached last; it stays when a member is opened again (status `doing`).

close.description: `auto`: reached by the engine when the last member is done; `manual`: by `milestone_set` status `done`.

done.description: Units done: a plan or project counts its tasks, the others one each.

complete.description: Every member is done (a milestone without members never is).

overdue.description: `due` is before today and it is neither done nor parked.

Paths.description: tasks.paths: the open learning paths of the vault or of an area (with `include_done` the finished ones too, `stage: done`, after them), each with its progress; no tree (that is tasks.path). Capability `paths`.

requires_cycles.description: The circles of requirements among the open paths and projects (those `check` reports as `requires-cycle`), each starting at its smallest id. Only when a path or project names a requirement. Capability `requires`.

done_projects.description: With `include_done`: the finished projects a requirement names, so that an arrow of a map ends in a box. Only when a path or project names a requirement. Capability `requires`.

PathDocument.description: tasks.path: one learning path with its body and its tree as a flat list in document order. Capability `path`.

body.description: The file after the frontmatter, untrusted text.

xp.description: The XP of the tree; only when a point carries XP. Capability `xp`.

levels.description: The lines of `## Level` in file order, the line of the whole path last; only when the file has the section. Capability `xp`.

schedule.description: The sessions of `## Zeitplan`: the points with planned hours that are a root or one level below, in file order, each with its hours, its result (the text after `Nachweis:`, `Aufgabe:` or `Ergebnis:` of its first such child) and its state (`partial`: some of its leaves closed). Only when the path has `hours`. Capability `path_hours`.

level_problems.description: The problems of `## Level` (`level-...` codes); with `levels`. Capability `xp`.

PathEntry.description: A learning path (`<area>/ROADMAP/paths/<slug>.md`): the head of its file, its progress over the leaves of its tree (optional ones apart, `optional`), its version.

has_tree.description: The file has a `## Lernpunkte` section.

points.description: The learning points of the tree, parents included.

xp.description: The XP of the tree; only when a point carries XP. Capability `xp`.

level.description: The level reached and what comes next; only when the file has levels. Capability `xp`.

levels.description: With `levels: true` of `tasks.paths`: every line of `## Level` in file order, the line of the whole path last; only when the file has the section. Capability `paths_levels`.

competence.description: The competences the path serves (`competence:`, ids of `<area>/ROADMAP/competences/<slug>.md`); only when the file names some. Capability `competences`.

competence_target.description: The stages the path aims at (`competence_target:`). Capability `competences`.

hours.description: The hours of the path; only when a point carries `{h=…}` or `{done_h=…}`. Capability `path_hours`.

Requires.description: What this path or project builds on (`requires:`), in the order of the file: `id`, `gate` (the file's `requires_gate`), `kind` (`path`, `project`, or `unknown`: no learning path or project of that id, `check` says `requires-unknown`) and `met` (the requirement is finished, closed into a Backlog). Only when the file names some. Capability `requires`.

RequiresGate.description: What a requirement that is not finished does (`requires_gate`): `soft` (the default) is a hint only (the item keeps its stage), `hard` keeps the path or project from being finished and the line of the whole path in `## Level` open. Capability `requires`.

WaitingOn.description: The open HARD requirements: the item cannot be finished while one is listed (a path's `level` then reads `finished: false`, the line of the whole path not reached). A path also lists the open hard requirements of its project, with `via` the project (a `requires` of a project holds for its paths). Empty: it may be finished. Present when the item names a requirement or inherits one. Capability `requires`.

PathStage.description: The stage of a path for a map of them: `done` (finished), `parked`, `waiting` (`waiting_on` not empty), `doing` (`status: doing`, or a point learned or seen), else `idle`. An open soft requirement never makes it wait. Capability `requires`.

PathOptional.description: The optional points of a tree (`{optional}` on a node, and its subtree), apart: `progress` and `xp` of the path leave them out, so they count for no level in percent and not for the path being finished; their XP count for a level in XP once earned (`xp` only when the tree has XP). Only when the tree has optional points. Capability `optional_points`.

PathProgress.description: Progress over leaves, counted apart: learned, seen, dropped, open (blocked ones counted as open and once more as blocked).

PathNode.description: One learning point of a tree. A parent has no mark of its own: its `derived` state comes from its leaves (learned, partial, open); `closed` when every leaf is (a parent with points that are not optional: every one of those).

index.description: Position in document order; `#<index>` names the point where it has no key.

line.description: The line of the body it stands on.

parent.description: The `index` of its parent; absent for a root.

state.description: Absent for an unknown mark (a tree problem).

promoted.description: The task the point was promoted to; it owns the point's state.

image.description: A file below `assets/` of the path; a client draws it as an image only.

progress.description: Over every leaf below the point, optional ones included (for showing it).

optional.description: The point is `{optional}` or below one: it counts for nothing that says how far the path is. Capability `optional_points`.

machine.description: The machines the point may be practised on (`{machine=a,b}` on it, else on the nearest parent that has one); absent: every machine. Capability `path_marks`.

safety.description: The point is `{safety}` or below one: closing it needs `ack` (it was read). Capability `path_marks`.

xp.description: The XP the leaf counts: its task's when it was promoted and the task has `xp`, else its own `{xp=N}`. Capability `xp`.

xp_suggest.description: A leaf without XP: a suggestion to fill a form in beforehand (never stored). Capability `xp`.

xp_progress.description: The XP below the point (its own for a leaf); only when the tree has XP. Capability `xp`.

PathXp.description: XP of a tree or a point (capability `xp`): learned counts in full, seen half (rounded down), dropped leaves sum and maximum.

possible.description: Every leaf but the dropped ones.

open.description: The XP of the open and blocked leaves.

PathLevelState.description: The levels of a path against its tree (capability `xp`): the highest level reached (0: none), the next one with what is missing, the rewards reached but not granted yet.

badge.description: The badge of the level reached, a file below `assets/badges/`; a client draws it as an image only.

percent.description: Of the possible XP; a tree without XP counts its points (learned 1, seen one half).

PathLevel.description: One line of `## Level` (capability `xp`): a threshold in XP or percent, or the line of the whole path (`kind: done`, `ref: done`).

line.description: The line of the body it stands on.

badge.description: As written; a file below `assets/badges/` (a client draws it as an image only).

reward.description: What one grants oneself, untrusted text.

PathEntryLevel.description: One line of `## Level` as `tasks.paths` carries it with `levels: true` (capability `paths_levels`): what `PathLevel` says, plus for a level not reached what is missing (`missing_xp`: the XP of a level in XP, or of a level in percent when the tree has XP; `missing_percent`: of a level in percent without XP, and of the line of the whole path), and from the series of the learning figures (`tasks.learn_history`) the day it was first reached (`reached_on`, only while it is reached) and its reward first granted (`given_on`, only while it is granted); absent before the series knew it.

badge.description: As written; a file below `assets/badges/` (a client draws it as an image only).

reward.description: What one grants oneself, untrusted text.

MeetingParse.description: tasks.meetingparse: one line of the quick capture read into a proposal of a meeting (capability `meeting_parse`). Nothing is written and no file is read: the front end shows the proposal in its form and sends `meeting_new` only when the person says so. `fields` are the keys `meeting_new` takes, as far as the line names them; `date` is always there (`assumed` holds `date` when the line named no day: today). `problems` are words that looked like a field but are none (`!soon`, `#nothing`); they are not in the title.

title.description: The words that are no field, in their order; may be empty.

online.description: An http or https address, untrusted text.

online_service.description: The service of `fields.online`, as a meeting entry tells it; absent without an address.

all_day.description: The line names no time (or says `ganztägig`).

MeetingDocument.description: tasks.meeting: one meeting with its body and the sections the engine reads. Capability `meeting`.

body.description: The file after the frontmatter, untrusted text.

href.description: The address, or the path below the meeting folder; a path of a machine is never named.

task.description: The task made of the line (`-> <id>`).

Status.description: The statuses of a task in `ROADMAP/tasks`. `done` is only seen on a task that was left there after it was finished (listed under `unlisted`).

WaitsKey.description: What a parked task waits for from outside (`waits_for`): one word of the vault's own, lower-case letters, digits and `-`. `none` is no key (it is what a filter calls a parked task without one).

ScaffoldRows.description: Acceptance lines by word of a list (a kind, a category or a scope).

Effort.description: A size (XS to XL) or a duration in days (`3d`, `0.5d`). `effort_days` is always the figure.

Etag.description: The version of a file: `sha256:` and 16 hex digits of the hash of its bytes.

Rev.description: What the vault looked like: `rev:` and 6 hex digits, from every task by id and etag.

Digest.description: The hash of the document's content (without `generated_at` and `engine`): the same vault gives the same digest.

Steps.description: The steps of the optional `## Plan` section; a dropped one is not counted.

Sheets.description: The test-sheet block testing.nvim writes into the task (`testing sheets report --tasks`), from its states line; absent without the block. `state` is the worst sheet (red, stale, never, inbox = green and waiting for a person's judgement, manual, green), `unknown` for a block without a states line. Nothing is run: it is what the last report wrote.

reason.description: Why the state is `unknown`: the block has no states line (an older testing.nvim), no state this engine knows is in it (a newer testing.nvim), or its markers are broken (two blocks, a begin without its end; testing.nvim does not write such a body). Absent otherwise.

Readiness.description: Where a task stands in the plan, from `blocked_by` alone.

stage.description: Absent for a task in a cycle.

rank.description: Position in plan order, 1 is first.

TaskEntry.description: One task. A broken task is still here (`valid: false`, `problems`); a field that is missing is unknown, never 0 (no `effort` means no `effort_days` and no `roi`).

meetings.description: The meetings that name the task (`tasks:` of a meeting file), the earliest first, at most 20. Only when there are some. Additive; capability `meetings`.

meetings_truncated.description: The task has more meetings than `meetings` names.

outcome_reason.description: Why it ended so (required by the engine for `seen` and `not-applicable`). Capability `outcome`.

xp.description: The XP of a learning task, as written; its learning point counts them after the outcome. Capability `xp`.

order.description: A tie-breaker inside a stage; a fraction slots a task in between.

roi.description: Value per effort day (never less than a quarter of a day), rounded to two places.

actor_written.description: True when `actor` is what the file says, absent when it was derived.

waits_for.description: What the task waits for from outside, as its file says; meant for a `parked` task (the engine drops it when the status leaves `parked`). Absent for a task that names none, and for a value that is no key (the `invalid-waits-for` problem).

remind.description: When to look at the task again (a reminder). The date only: whether it is due is for the reader to say, so that a digest does not change with the day.

remind_at.description: The local time of day (HH:MM) the reminder of the `remind` day is sent; only beside `remind`. Without it the reminder goes with the notice of the day. Additive.

remind_to.description: The e-mail addresses the reminder of the `remind` day is sent to (only valid ones, only beside `remind`). Additive.

due.description: When the task is due (optional). Not the reminder: `remind` brings a task back, `due` is a deadline. The date only; whether it is overdue is for the reader to say.

start.description: The earliest day to begin (optional). Never after `due`.

claim.description: Somebody works on the task (optional; capability `claims`): who, since when, until when (UTC). `expired` is the engine's judgement when the document was made; a reader that keeps it compares `until` with its own clock. An expired claim counts as free.

repeat.description: A routine (optional): every N days, weeks, months or years (`8w`). Finishing the task starts the next round. Capability `repeat`. With capability `repeat_steps` also a ladder of 2 to 12 intervals (`1w,4w,12w`): each round takes the next interval, the last round ends the routine.

repeat_step.description: A ladder (`repeat: 1w,4w,12w`): the round the open task is, 1-based; absent: 1 (capability `repeat_steps`).

repeat_after.description: A routine that starts when something is finished (capability `repeat_steps`): a task or learning path id (`<area>/<slug>`) or a point of a path (`<area>/<slug>#<key>`). While it has no `due` it waits; the finish writes due = that day + the first interval.

repeat_from.description: Where the next round counts from: the day the round was finished (`done`, the default) or the due date of the finished round (`due`, a fixed rhythm).

project.description: The project the task belongs to directly, instead of a plan (capability `projects`).

scope.description: What the task touches (optional, only when the task names a scope).

late_blockers.description: The open blockers (`blocked_by` hard, `after` soft) due after the task begins: after its `start`, else after its `due` (`against` says which). Only when there are some (capability `late_blockers`); a parked task has none.

refs.description: As written, but a path of the machine shows as `<external>/<name>`.

links.description: Web addresses of the task (`http://` or `https://`), apart from `refs`. Only when the task lists any.

open_questions.description: How many questions of the `## Offene Fragen` section of the task are not answered; absent when none is open.

AreaGroup.description: An area group (`<vault>/area-groups.json`, in Neovim also `setup({ area_groups })`): a filter name that stands for several areas. The methods `list`, `order`, `next` and `finished` take a group name for `area` too (`check` takes one area); a write target never is one. Only groups in force are listed (an area of the same name wins).

members.description: The areas of the vault the group stands for, sorted.

Hello.description: tasks.hello: what this engine is and can do. Reads no task.

schemas.description: The versions of the contract this engine speaks.

today.description: The day the engine counts as today: the local day of its machine (a `due:` or `remind:` day has come when it is this day or earlier). Additive.

time.description: The local time of day of the engine's machine, HH:MM, beside `today`: a caller without a time zone sends the reminders of the day from an hour of the person's choice. Additive.

capabilities.description: What it can answer; show only what is listed.

intents.description: The intents tasks takes (`wkd-intent/1`, appkit/schemas/wkd-intent/1): a sender offers only these actions and modes. Additive; capability `intent`.

present.description: The vault has a marker file `tasks-vault.json` (valid or refused).

layout_version.description: Version of the folder layout the file names; absent when there is no valid file.

problem.description: Why the file is refused (every other call then fails with `invalid_argument` and this message); no path.

marker.description: The marker file of the vault (schemas/tasks-vault/1). Additive; capability `vault_marker`.

enums.description: The ranges of the fields, from the engine, so that nobody hard-codes them.

meeting_status.description: The statuses of a meeting. Additive; capability `meetings`.

meeting_icon.description: The icons a meeting may name (`icon`). Additive; capability `meetings`. The same list as `icon_word`.

icon_word.description: The words an `icon` of kind `word` may be (a front end draws its own sign for each). Additive; capability `icon`.

online_service.description: The services the address of a meeting is told as (`online_service`); `link` for any other. Additive; capability `meetings`.

scaffold.description: The fixed acceptance lines a new task can start with, by kind, category and scope. A client joins the rows of what applies, each id once, in the order kind, category, scope (the order of the lists above); `implied` adds the rows of the named scopes when the kind and one of the categories match. The text follows the language of the task's headings (`de` or `en`).

Snapshot.description: tasks.snapshot: one scan, one `rev`: counts, areas, the plan's head, the plan files and every open task with its readiness.

views_rev.description: What the saved views looked like: the `rev` of `tasks.views` (`rev:` and 6 hex digits, from every file of a view by id and etag). A view changed outside changes it (and the digest), not `rev`: a reader that shows the views reads them again when it differs from the one it read.

area_groups.description: The area groups in force with their members; left out when the vault has none.

reminders.description: Finished tasks that carry a reminder (`remind`), the oldest date first, at most 100. An open task's reminder is on its entry; a finished task is not in `tasks`, and a reminder is most often set when a task is finished.

unlisted.description: Task files in `ROADMAP/tasks` that are not open work: a finished task left there, a status nobody knows.

unknown_effort.description: Tasks on the path without an effort (counted as one day each).

conflict_groups.description: Tasks of one stage that name the same file: not parallel work. A list of objects (a tuple would not survive the TypeScript generator).

project.description: The project the plan belongs to (capability `projects`).

phase.description: The stage of that project the plan belongs to.

etag.description: The version of the plan file, for `if_match` of `plan_set` (capability `projects`); absent for a file that cannot be read.

projects.description: The open project files (capability `projects`): a project groups plans and may hold tasks of its own.

etag.description: The version of the project file, for `if_match` of `project_set`; absent for a file that cannot be read.

plans.description: The ids of the open plans of the project, sorted.

incomplete.description: Folders that could not be read: the answer may be incomplete.

List.description: tasks.list: one page of tasks in plan order, or in the order the request named (`sort`).

NamedList.description: A named list: a filter and an order under a name. `options` are the option words of the command line (`tasks list --effort=<=S --sort=roi`), a switch is present as `true` and absent when off; a list the engine rejects is not here but in `notes` of the document. `summary` is the one line the engine shows for it (its description, else the words).

NamedLists.description: tasks.lists: the named lists of the engine, read only: the built-in ones, the ones saved with the editor and the ones of the configuration (the later source wins by name), by name. `notes` tell what had to be left out (a rejected definition, a shadowed list, a state file that cannot be read), in the engine's words and without a path of this machine.

Order.description: tasks.order: the ids of the open tasks in the order the request named (`sort`; "default" is the plan's order), all in one document.

Estimate.description: tasks.estimate: the figures of an estimate for some open tasks, also as they would be with other efforts and values (`assume`; nothing is written). The same figures as `estimate` in the snapshot, with the range of the sizes.

range.description: The sum with every size at its low and at its high end: without it the sum looks more exact than it is.

assumed.description: How many of the tasks were taken with assumed values.

PlanCompareRow.description: One open plan of tasks.plan_compare. `tasks`: its open and finished tasks, the open ones by readiness state. `effort`: open days (with the range of the sizes), finished days, open tasks without an effort. `path`: the critical path of the plan's open tasks alone (a blocker outside the plan takes no part). `weekly_done`: members finished in each of the last `weeks` weeks, oldest first (the last week ends `today`). `forecast_weeks`: weeks the open tasks would still take, `low` at the pace of the best of those weeks, `high` at their average; absent when nothing was finished in them or nothing is open. `phase_now`: the first stage of the plan's `phase_order` that still has an open task. `value`: over the open tasks, the sum of their `value`, the average of those that carry one (two decimals, absent when none does) and how many carry none; `prio`: the best (lowest) prio among them. `areas`: the plan's own area, then the other areas it names (a plan that names none is one of its own area). `target_due`: the `due` of the plan's `target` task while it is open, `due_in_days` from `today` (negative when it has passed), and `forecast_late`: `forecast_weeks.high` weeks from `today` end after that day (only with both a due day and a forecast).

PlanCompare.description: tasks.plan_compare (capability `plan_compare`): the open plans side by side, one row each in the order of the vault (`ids` narrows it to some). The figures are the engine's; a page that compares plans only sorts and draws them. The finished tasks lie outside the revision, as in `tasks.finished`.

PlanFor.description: tasks.planfor: the tasks one task needs before it can start (`needs`) or the tasks that wait for it (`unlocks`), with the hard edges between them, in the order of their distance from the task. The same tasks as `plan --for`.

total.description: All the tasks in the graph; `nodes` holds at most 500 of them.

from.description: The task that has to be finished first.

cycles.description: The cycles whose members are all among `nodes`.

Check.description: tasks.check: the rule check of the vault (`tasks check`), with `stale: refs` also the open tasks that name a file which changed after the task was updated. It reads every task file: a client runs it as a job.

tasks.description: Task files read, open and finished.

total.description: All the findings; `findings` holds at most 1000 of them.

id.description: The task the finding is about, when there is one.

notes.description: What could not be checked (git missing, a budget used up).

Bodies.description: tasks.bodies: the text of many tasks, a page at a time, for a reader that searches it. Its `rev` is that of the snapshot of the same vault.

body.description: The file after the frontmatter, untrusted text.

next_offset.description: Absent on the last page; where to go on when a page ended early (it holds as many bytes as a page may).

AgentAnswer.description: tasks.agent_answer (capability agent_answer): the answer of an agent's job (kind review-done or prepare-decision) taken apart for one task by the rules of :Tasks agent, as the sections a caller writes with set_section after a yes. Nothing is written. The texts are untrusted.

sections.description: In the order to write them: the heading (one line, '## ' and a word) and the text below it, trimmed.

follow_up.description: review-done: the follow-up task the review proposes (create it only after a yes of its own).

questions_added.description: prepare-decision: whether the open questions are among the sections (only when the task has none of its own).

TaskDocument.description: tasks.task: one task with its body and steps.

body.description: The file after the frontmatter, untrusted text.

finished.description: Capability task_finished: the call named finished, and this is the finished task of the id, read from its area's Backlog/ (no readiness, no rounds).

questions.description: The questions of the `## Offene Fragen` / `## Open questions` section, in the order written; empty without the section. A question is answered when exactly one option is ticked; `answer` writes it.

key.description: `q1`; absent for a question written without one (the first `answer` gives it one). `answer` takes the key.

rounds.description: Only for a routine (`task.repeat`; capability `rounds`): its finished rounds, newest first, at most 100. A round is a task file below `<area>/Backlog/` that carries `repeat` and shares the routine's slug without the due date a round adds. `done` is the date in its file name (absent without one). The rounds lie outside the revision, as in `tasks.finished`.

rounds_truncated.description: Present (true) when the routine has more finished rounds than `rounds` holds.

Next.description: tasks.next: what to start, with the reason; or why there is nothing.

cdx.description: Ready tasks an AI session could take, apart from yours.

later.description: Ready tasks left out because their `start` day has not come yet; absent when none.

claimed.description: Ready tasks left out because somebody else has claimed them (capability `claims`); absent when none.

left_out.description: Ready tasks left out because they are of a category the request named in `not_category` (capability `next_not_category`); absent when none.

empty.description: Present when there is no task to start: which kind of nothing it is. `all_done` is only said when nothing is open at all.

waits_for.description: Of the parked tasks: how many wait for each `waits_for` key. Left out when none of them names one.

Areas.description: tasks.areas: the areas of the vault with their open counts.

area_groups.description: The area groups in force with their members; left out when the vault has none.

FindMatch.description: A task that names a ref: the ref, the task (id, area, status) and where it is, `open` (ROADMAP) or `done` (Backlog). Never a path. A meeting (`kind` `meeting`, capability `meeting_ops`) matches a task id it names in `tasks:` or behind a follow-up; it is `open` while planned.

Find.description: tasks.find: the tasks, open and finished, whose `refs` name one of the refs asked for (capability `find`). Open tasks first, then by id.

Intent.description: tasks.intent: what tasks did with an intent `wkd-intent/1` (capability `intent`): `would_create` (a dry run), `created` (with `yes`), `exists` (a task holds the ref `testing-finding:<fp>` already: `matches`), `shown` or `not_found` (`tasks.show`). A refused intent is an error (`invalid_argument`, every problem in the message), nothing written.

Waits.description: tasks.waits: what the parked tasks wait for, of the vault or of one area (or area group). `keys` are the `waits_for` keys in use, the one with the most tasks first (then by name), each with its number of parked tasks and their areas. `parked` counts every parked task: the ones of `keys`, `without_reason` (parked by choice, no `waits_for`) and `invalid` (a `waits_for` that is no key, the `invalid-waits-for` finding). Same `rev` as the snapshot of the same state.

incomplete.description: Folders that could not be read: the answer may be incomplete.

FinishedItem.description: A finished task of `Backlog/`: what the engine knows without the plan (a finished task has no readiness). `done` is the day in the file's name; absent for a file without one.

outcome_reason.description: Why it ended so (required by the engine for `seen` and `not-applicable`). Capability `outcome`.

xp.description: The XP of a learning task, as written; its learning point counts them after the outcome. Capability `xp`.

FinishedStats.description: What the finished tasks add up to, over ALL that match the window (not the page). A task that does not carry the field has a row without the key (missing means unknown). The rows of `by_month` and `by_week` are oldest first, the others the biggest first.

effort_days.description: The sum of the efforts that are written down.

without_effort.description: Tasks without an effort (not counted in `effort_days`).

Finished.description: tasks.finished: the finished tasks of the Backlogs, newest first, one page, and what ALL that match add up to. Asked with `since` and `until` (days, both included) it covers the tasks `done` ran for in that window; the area is the one the file is in now.

undated.description: Finished files (of the area asked for) without a `YYYY-MM-DD_` in the name: they are in the figures only when no window is asked for.

HistoryPoint.description: One day (or one week, named by its Monday) of `tasks.history`. `done` and `created` are what the files say about the day and are always there. The level (`open` and the fields beside it) is the sum over the areas of the last row each of them has up to that day: absent before the first row (unknown, never 0), all of it or none. `recorded` is false for a level that was carried over (no row of the areas asked for was written on that day).

done.description: Tasks finished on the day (the date in the name of the Backlog file); for a week their sum.

created.description: Tasks, open or finished, whose `created` is the day; for a week their sum.

by_state.description: By readiness, the figures of the plan head of the snapshot (`plan.summary`).

with_effort.description: Open tasks that carry an effort.

with_value.description: Open tasks that carry a value.

effort_days.description: The sum of the written efforts of the open tasks.

value.description: The sum of the written values of the open tasks.

History.description: tasks.history (capability `history`): the figures of the overview over time, one point per day or week of the window `since`..`until` (both included), oldest first. The levels come from the series the engine writes down below `_Telemetry/history/` of the vault (a row per day and area whose figures changed; `first` and `last` are the first and last day that has a row of the areas asked for, absent without a series). The series lies outside the revision, as the finished tasks do.

area.description: The area or area group asked for; absent for the whole vault.

incomplete.description: What was skipped: a line of the series that is no row (`<file>:<line>: <why>`, relative to the vault), a folder that could not be read.

LinkEdge.description: One link between the open tasks of two areas, seen from the task it starts at. `to` is the other task (`blocked_by`, `after`) or the plan (`plan`); `ref` is the ref as written (`refs`).

Links.description: tasks.links: where the areas hang together. A link is a `blocked_by` or `after` to an open task of another area, a ref that names another area (`lib.nvim@803de65`, `lib.nvim:anchor`; a path says nothing about the repo), or a plan whose open tasks lie in several areas. `pairs` groups the edges by the two areas (`a` sorts before `b`, the busiest pair first); `tasks` lists, for every open task that touches two or more areas, the areas it touches (its own and those of every link it is part of, in both directions). The edges of the pairs are cut at 2000 (`truncated`); `edge_count`, the counts and `tasks` cover all of them.

Groupings.description: tasks.groupings: the fields the open tasks can be grouped by, with the values each can have and how a reader writes it. `status`, `prio`, `actor`, `kind`, `effort` and `value` are the model's; `tags`, `plan`, `phase` and `project` (derived: the project of the task's plan, or its own) are the ones the open tasks name (at most 200, `truncated` says the rest); `area` is the areas of the vault; `state` and `cross` are derived (`cross`: `several` for a task `tasks.links` names among the tasks that touch two or more areas, else `one`). `mode` says which operation writes the field: `set` (a field of the file), `tags` (the list of tags: leaving one and taking another is one `set` of the whole list) or `move_area`; a field without `mode` is read only. The same `rev` as the snapshot of the same vault.

View.description: One saved view: a selection (which tasks), a grouping (by which field, a matrix by a second one) and how it is drawn. It holds no task and no rule. `etag` is the version of its file: a change is made on it (`view_save`, `view_delete`).

group_by2.description: The field of the rows of a matrix (never the field of the columns).

collapsed.description: The groups that are folded (the values as `tasks.groupings` names them).

ViewSelect.description: Which tasks a view shows: every list narrows (an empty list does not), `query` is a word the title must hold.

Views.description: tasks.views: the saved views of the vault (`<area>/ROADMAP/views/<slug>.md`), sorted by id. A file that cannot be read as a view is no view but a line of `problems`. The `rev` is that of the views, not of the tasks.

Error.description: tasks.error: what went wrong, in a code that is stable. `message` carries no path of the machine.

ErrorCode.description: Why something failed, in a word that is stable. A reader treats a word it does not know as `internal`.

Icon.description: What an item stands for (`icon:`; capability `icon`): an emoji (one grapheme cluster), an image below `assets/` of the item's folder, or a word of `hello.enums.icon_word`. Absent when the item has none.

Ci.description: The CI state of a task's commits beside `commits` (capability `ci`): pending (pushed, no verdict yet), green (the CI passed on every system) or red (it failed). Absent: not known.

Outcome.description: How a finished task ended beside `status: done` (capability `outcome`): learned, seen (looked at, not done) or not-applicable. Absent: done as meant.

Point.description: The learning point a task was promoted from: `<container id>#<key>`, the container a learning path or a task with `## Lernpunkte` (capability `outcome`).

Cover.description: A large picture of the item (`cover:`; capability `icon`): an image (png, jpg, jpeg, webp, svg) below `assets/` of its folder. Absent when it has none.

PlanLinks.description: The web addresses of a plan or project file (`links:`, http/https only; capability `plan_links`). Absent when it has none.

PlanFolder.description: The plan or project file is in its folder form (`<slug>/<slug>.md`, made by `attach` or `folderize`): the other files of that folder are its assets. Absent for a plain file.

PlanAssets.description: The files in the folder of a plan or project (folder form only), relative to that folder (`assets/screenshots/shot.png`), sorted; at most 100.

PlanAssetsTruncated.description: The folder holds more than the 100 `assets` listed.

OperationError.description: Why an operation did not happen. `details` names ids, keys and values (`expected` and `actual` of a conflict, the `problems` of a refused relation, `field`/`value`/`char`/`suggestion` of a word that is no kebab-case word), never a path.

hint.description: What to do instead, in words (`milestone_set` that would keep a complete milestone of `close: auto` open: set `close: manual`).

field.description: A word that must be kebab-case (a phase, an entry of the phases) was not: the field it was given for (`phase`).

value.description: The word as it was given.

char.description: The first character that is not allowed (`-` when the hyphens are wrong); absent for an empty word.

suggestion.description: A word that would do: umlauts and ß written out (`ü` -> `ue`), lower case, other characters as single hyphens. Absent when nothing usable is left.

LevelsSpec.description: The levels of a learning path as `path_levels` takes them: the levels in order (thresholds rising within a unit) and the line for the whole path. An empty `list` without `done` removes them.

list.description: At most 20 levels (no `maxItems`: the type generator would make tuples of it).

badge.description: A picture below `assets/badges/` of the path.

given.description: The reward was granted (only with a reward).

Inverse.description: The operation that undoes a change: send it as a new operation (its `if_match` is the version the change left). A key the change added is `null` in the patch of a `set`.

xp.description: `node_set` that wrote XP: the XP the point had (capability `xp`).

ack.description: `node_set` that reopens a point closed under `{safety}`: the inverse closes it again and carries the ack (capability `path_marks`).

xp_clear.description: `node_set` that wrote XP on a point that had none: remove them again (capability `xp`).

given.description: `path_reward`: whether the reward was granted before.

levels.description: `path_levels`: the levels the path had (capability `path_levels`); absent when its `## Level` held lines a spec cannot carry.

container.description: `unpromote`: the path or task the learning point is in.

point.description: `node_set`, `unpromote`: the learning point, its key or `#<index>`.

note.description: `node_set` that wrote a note: the note the point had, `""` when it had none (capability `node_note`).

section.description: `tick_step` of a meeting: the section of the item (`agenda`, `followups`).

present.description: `meeting_attend`: whether the participant is to be ticked present.

done.description: `tick_step`: whether the step is to be ticked (true) or open (false).

clear.description: `answer`: true when no option was ticked, the question was open.

body.description: `set_body`: the text below the frontmatter that the task had.

heading.description: `set_section`: the heading of the section that was replaced.

text.description: `set_section`: the text the section had below its heading.

to_area.description: `move_area`: the area the task came from (`id` is the id it has now).

view.description: `view_save`: the view as it was (a `view_save` with it puts it back).

MovePlan.description: What moving a task to another area would do and break (stage 1 of `move_area`: a report, nothing is written).

references.description: Places that name the old id and would dangle.

ResultEntry.description: What happened to one operation of a request, in the order they were sent. A failed operation does not stop the others.

without_result.description: `meeting_close`: the meeting has no `## Ergebnis` afterwards (allowed: a hint for the front end).

items.description: `meeting_followups`: one entry per follow-up line it worked on: the task made of it (`id`) or why not (`error`).

preview.description: `board_save`: the preview of the board below its folder (`assets/boards/<name>.svg`).

etag.description: `board_save`: the version of the board file now (send it as `if_match` to replace it).

created.description: `board_save`: true when the board was new, false when it replaced one. A meeting operation on an occurrence of a series without a file: true when the operation made (a dry run: would make) its file (capability `meeting_series`).

outcome.description: `would_*` is what a dry run says; `blocked` is a move that cannot be made.

node.description: `node_set`: the learning point as it is now (capability `node_set`).

xp.description: `node_set` that wrote XP: the point's own XP now; absent when removed (capability `xp`).

progress.description: `node_set`: the progress of the path after the change.

level.description: `path_reward`: the level as it is now (capability `path_reward`).

promoted_from.description: `promote`: the learning point the new task came from, `<container>#<key>` (capability `promote`).

moved.description: `promote`: the lines of the point's subtree that moved into the task.

repointed.description: `promote`, `unpromote`: the open tasks of points promoted below the moved one, whose `point` now names the new container.

container.description: `unpromote`: the path or task the point is in.

restore.description: What a reorder wrote: these `set` operations give every file it wrote its old `order` back (send them all instead of `inverse`, which only restores the place: a task that had no `order` would keep one, and the neighbours the move numbered stay numbered).

changed_ids.description: Ids whose files this operation wrote (a dry run: none).

index.description: What happened to the generated index of the area, once for the whole request.

slug.description: `plan_new`: the file name (without `.md`) the plan got or would get.

renamed.description: `plan_new`: the slug asked for was taken, so another one was chosen.

asset.description: `attach`: the path of the new asset below the task folder, e.g. `assets/shot.png`.

link.description: `attach`: the Markdown that links the asset (an image gets `![name](path)`), to put into the task.

rows.description: `history_record`: the rows written into the series (a dry run: that would be written).

learn_rows.description: `history_record`: the rows written into the series of the learning paths (`_Telemetry/history/learn-YYYY-MM.jsonl`; a dry run: that would be written). Capability `learn_history`.

learn_file.description: `history_record`: the month file of the learning series, relative to the vault. Capability `learn_history`.

projects_closed.description: The projects this finish closed after the plan (capability `projects`).

milestones_reached.description: The milestones this operation reached: their last member was finished by it (capability `milestones`; only when there is one).

milestones_reopened.description: The reached milestones this operation set back to `doing`: a member of theirs is open again; `reached` stays (capability `milestones`; only when there is one).

routines_started.description: `done`, `node_set`, `path_close`: the routines that waited for what this operation finished (`repeat_after`) and got their first `due` (capability `repeat_steps`; only when there is one). Their ids are in `changed_ids`.

point.description: `done`: the learning point the task was promoted from, set to the state of the finish (capability `outcome`).

held.description: The point was left as it was: it is on or under a `{safety}` mark and the finish carried no `ack`; the notes say so (capability `path_marks`).

new_id.description: `move_area`: the id the task has after the move.

rewritten.description: `move_area`: the places that named the old id and now name the new one.

Result.description: tasks.result: the answer to a request of `tasks-ops/1`, one entry per operation. `ok` is true only when every operation was.

DonePreview.description: tasks.donepreview: what finishing a task would do, with nothing written, and the `confirm` token that `done` needs for exactly this version of the file.

already.description: The task is finished already: nothing to confirm.

outcome_reason.description: Why it ended so (required by the engine for `seen` and `not-applicable`). Capability `outcome`.

closes_plan.description: The plan this finish closes: the task is its last open member.

closes_project.description: The project this finish closes after that: no other plan (a parked one does not count) and no task of its own is open (capability `projects`).

ends_routine.description: The task is the last round of a ladder (`repeat: 1w,4w,12w`): the finish starts no next round (capability `repeat_steps`; only when true).

next_round.description: Present when the task is a routine (`repeat`): the due date of the round the finish starts.

freed.description: Open tasks that wait on nothing but this one.
